general_information.Description: The course is organized around five parts: 1) Entrepreneurs and ideas: the basis of small business; 2) Small business paths and plans; 3) Marketing in the small business; 4) Cash, Accounting, Finance in the small business; 5) Management and Organization in the small business. Particular emphasis will be placed on internal, external business analyis, business strategies, business plans, marketing plans, asset management, and human resource management. Vigorous class discussions, cases, activities, along with group projects and self quizzes will provide the basis for the learning environment in the classroom.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance

Evaluate the effectiveness of different entrepreneurial strategies

assessments.Question Type: Option 1: A group of four or five students will produce a real business plan for one company. The input for the assignment must be based on your interview, observation, market research, internal, external analysis, data gathering through primary and secondaty data. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic. Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
